Control Blender with natural language and multi-agent AI workflows! 🪄🤖

Have you ever wished you could bridge text-based AI models directly into spatial 3D design software? The disconnect between LLMs and complex 3D environments slows down procedural pipelines and rapid prototyping. 

The Blender AI MCP Addon solves this by integrating a Model Context Protocol server and a visual companion workspace directly into Blender 4.2+. It empowers AI assistants to inspect live scenes, execute `bpy` scripts, manipulate objects, assign materials, and chain multi-step workflows seamlessly.

Key Features Built for Tech Enthusiasts and AI Engineers:
🔹 Built-in MCP Server: Enables external clients like OpenCode to securely connect and issue authenticated commands to Blender.
🔹 Multi-Agent Task Chains: Features Manager, Worker, and Reviewer roles that autonomously break down, execute, and validate complex 3D scene operations sequentially.
🔹 21+ Built-In Scene Tools: Comprehensive suite spanning scene inspection, procedural object creation, material editing, viewport screenshot capture, and asset search/import.
🔹 Flexible Architecture: Supports OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, and local Ollama instances with visual model selection.

Whether you are an AI engineer building advanced tool-use workflows, a technical artist automating batch-export pipelines, or a developer looking for a blueprint on how to expose local software APIs to LLMs via the Model Context Protocol, this repository is a must-explore.

Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/bookwjitchieni1986/blender-ai-mcp-addon

Stop treating your AI coding assistants like glorified autocomplete tools. 🚀

If you are tired of disjointed AI workflows, constant manual prompting for basic planning, and losing context between sessions, it is time to level up your development stack. 

Meet ECC: the operating system and harness optimizer that turns AI coding assistants into a unified, self-improving engineering system. 

The Problem:
Modern AI coding tools like Claude Code and Cursor are powerful, but their workflows are fragmented. They lack structured engineering frameworks, struggle with context window optimization, and don't retain crucial project knowledge across sessions. 

How ECC Solves It:
ECC embeds structured engineering frameworks—like planning, test-driven development (TDD), self-review, and continuous learning—directly into your agent's environment. It acts as a comprehensive harness optimizer that gives your AI team persistent memory and automated verification workflows.

Key Features Built for Power Users:
• Comprehensive Toolset: Armed with 72 specialized agents, 328 skills, and 99 command shims covering planning, review, build repair, security, architecture, and domain-specific engineering.
• AgentShield Security: Integrated security scanning to ensure secure coding patterns and protect against vulnerabilities during autonomous execution.
• Cross-Platform Compatibility: Native plugins for Claude Code and Codex, plus adapters for Cursor, Gemini, Zed, and GitHub Copilot.
• Continuous Learning: Memory structures that allow agents to remember what matters and turn repeated wins into reusable skills and workflows.

Stop wasting time on manual structural prompts. Install ECC and establish a consistent, repeatable engineering lifecycle where your AI agents automatically test implementations, review their own work, and retain project memory.

Tired of Windows bloat, heavy background telemetry, and resource-hogging shell components slowing down your dev machine? 

Meet WinRust—a complete reimagining of core Windows shell components like the taskbar, file manager, and task manager built entirely in memory-safe Rust. It replaces legacy utilities with lean, native alternatives that deliver dramatic speedups while slashing your resource footprint.

Why systems programmers and power users are loving it:
⚡ Up to 99% faster file search using a pre-made MFT index for high-performance NTFS querying.
🧠 Ultra-lightweight shell using roughly 87% less RAM than the stock Windows Explorer stack.
🚫 Real debloating that strips out background telemetry and AI features like Copilot and Recall.
🚀 A native custom file copier and multi-core ZIP/7z extraction engine built for blazing-fast transfers.
🛠️ Comprehensive system tuning to optimize NTFS performance and manage boot tasks.

Whether you want to reclaim your hardware for heavy local compilation or study advanced systems programming patterns for low-level Win32 API interaction in Rust, this repository is a must-see.

Check it out on GitHub and reclaim your system resources:
https://github.com/Lemxy/WinRust

🎮 What if you could run Xbox Series X software natively on Windows without an active emulation loop? 

Meet Xbox2Windows—an experimental framework pushing the absolute boundaries of hardware emulation and static recompilation! 🚀

The Problem:
Targeting proprietary console architectures like the Xbox Series X|S (Scarlett) usually requires heavy, resource-intensive real-time emulation. This project takes a radically different approach, investigating how to translate source-built x64 PE machine code and custom graphics pipelines directly for native x64 Windows execution.

✨ Key Features:
• Offline x64 CPU & Function Translation: Handles direct calls, switch dispatch jump tables, instruction lifting for flags, and cross-DLL imports by name or ordinal without runtime overhead.
• Advanced Graphics Pipeline: Translates console-specific gfx1013 pixel shaders into desktop-compatible HLSL/DXIL, complete with FidelityFX upscaler integration and BC7 texture decoding.
• Windows Runtime Simulation: Features image mapping without LoadLibrary, custom heap allocation routing, and structured exception handling (SEH) with TLS-callback and entry-point notifications.
• Hardware Validation: Extensive compute, ray tracing, and BVH differential testing across modern NVIDIA and AMD GPU architectures.

🛠️ Built for emulator developers, reverse engineers, systems programmers, and graphics engineers who want to study complex instruction lifting, Win32 heap memory mapping, and console-to-desktop shader bridging.

Dive into the code and explore the architecture today:
https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows

Tired of browsers that hog all your RAM and compromise your data? Meet Yab: a fast, native macOS and iOS browser built to challenge bloated web-based alternatives by combining WebKit and Chromium engines with built-in AI agents and end-to-end encrypted sync. 🚀

Modern browsers have become heavy, resource-hungry resource hogs that drain batteries and lack true privacy. Yab solves this by offering a lightweight, native application that minimizes UI overhead while packing advanced developer capabilities.

Here is why developers and power users are checking it out:
⚡ Dual-Engine Architecture: Runs on WebKit by default with native Apple Silicon support for Chromium per tab or site, complete with Chrome extensions and DevTools.
🤖 Integrated AI Agents: Operates safely in isolated tabs using your existing provider sign-ins with strict user authorization checks for sensitive actions.
🛡️ Advanced Privacy: Built-in pre-request ad blocking and persistent element hiding for ultimate performance.
🔒 Secure Sync: Optional end-to-end encrypted synchronization across all your macOS and iOS devices.

For developers, Yab serves as an incredible blueprint for building high-performance, native Swift applications. Explore the architecture, study the keychain integration, and see how to implement local-first E2EE sync firsthand.
